research.pitfalls:
1. FIXING THE TIMESTAMP WITHOUT FIXING THE ANCHOR IS A NO-OP. Making the header a pure function of (anchor vertex, parent header) only helps if every node picks the same anchor. ordering.rs:503-510 picks the anchor by round-robin over whichever leader vertex happens to be in the LOCAL dag, :487-491 partitions committed rounds by local arrival order, and :755-772 silently skips missing parents. Land this fix without BLOCKER-3/4 and you have traded a divergent timestamp for a divergent anchor — the same fork, now harder to spot because the header looks deterministic. Sequence: ordering determinism first (or same PR), timestamp second.

2. THE CLASS-A / CLASS-B SPLIT IS THE WHOLE GAME, AND IT IS EASY TO GET BACKWARDS. Any rule that reads `SystemTime::now()` is non-deterministic and therefore CANNOT be a validity rule — it may only gate gossip admission. sync/src/lib.rs:287-297 already violates this today by applying `now + 30` to replayed history. The failure is asymmetric and nasty: because sync/src/lib.rs:264 wedges on `prev_hash` mismatch, one clock-skewed rejection does not merely skip a block, it halts that node's sync forever. Conversely, do not "fix" it by deleting the drift check from dag.rs:659-676 — that one is correctly placed and is the only thing bounding hash-grinding surface at admission.

3. SWITCHING TO MILLISECOND RESOLUTION SILENTLY MULTIPLIES LEADER-ELECTION GRINDING BY 1000x. This is AINCORE-specific and does not exist in the reference chains. `finality_digest` (ordering.rs:430 `fold_finality_digest`, :623) folds committed VERTEX HASHES, and `vertex.calculate_hash()` includes `vertex.timestamp`. That digest seeds `beacon_challenge` (:278) -> `step1_beacon` -> `vdf_seed` -> `get_leader_with_fallback` (:730). So an anchor author can already grind its vertex timestamp to bias future leader election — the code's own H-2 comment (ordering.rs ~:702) concedes the Step-1 base is proposer-biasable via chosen content, but does not name the timestamp as one of the free dimensions. At 1-second granularity within a 30s drift window the search space is ~30 candidates; adopting CometBFT's `parent + 1ms` tick without thought turns that into ~30,000 cheap candidates per proposal. Mitigations, in order of strength: (a) go to STEP 4's stake-weighted median so a single author cannot choose the value at all — this is precisely why Sui and CometBFT use a median rather than the leader's own clock; (b) quantize the timestamp that enters the header/beacon (floor to 1s or 250ms) so grinding space stays small; (c) exclude the timestamp from the beacon preimage. Do NOT rely on the 30s drift bound alone.

4. "DROP THE LOCAL CLOCK" IS NOT THE SAME AS "DROP THE CLOCK READ AT THE AUTHOR." Every reference chain reads a wall clock somewhere — CometBFT at precommit, PBTS/Aptos at proposal, Sui in each block. The invariant is that the read happens ONCE, at a signed and replicated author-side point, and is never repeated at commit/replay/verification. dag.rs:429 (vertex timestamp) is a legitimate author-side read and must stay; consensus/blockchain/src/lib.rs:56 (header construction, run independently by every node after commit) is the illegitimate one. Deleting the wrong one costs you the only real clock in the system.

5. CLAMPING vs REJECTING IS A LIVENESS DECISION, AND REJECTING WEDGES A DAG CHAIN. Sui deliberately CLAMPS (`.max(last_commit_timestamp_ms)`) rather than rejecting a regressing median, because in a DAG the commit is already decided by the time the timestamp is computed — rejecting there means refusing to commit an already-ordered anchor, i.e. a permanent stall of exactly the BLOCKER-3 shape. Apply the same reasoning to the upper bound: `derive_block_timestamp` clamps to `parent + MAX_BLOCK_TS_DELTA`; it must not return an error. Reserve rejection for the gossip-admission path (Class A), where refusing a vertex is cheap and recoverable.

6. STRICT MONOTONICITY BREAKS ON EMPTY/HEARTBEAT BLOCKS UNLESS YOU DECIDE THE NIL CASE EXPLICITLY. AINCORE mines heartbeat blocks with empty payloads (dag.rs comment at :890: "We execute even if empty to trigger Block Rewards"). Aptos handles the analogous case by giving NIL blocks EXACTLY the parent's timestamp (`assert!(now == timestamp)`) and exempting them from the future bound. AINCORE's heartbeat blocks are proposer-attributed and carry rewards, so they are NOT Aptos-NIL — they should take the strictly-increasing path. But note the interaction with the reward path: a `parent_ts + 1` floor combined with heartbeat mining means the chain clock advances at least 1s per block regardless of real time, so at high block rates the committed clock can drift AHEAD of real time. With MAX_BLOCK_TS_DELTA = 300s that drift is bounded per block but unbounded cumulatively — which is exactly why `epoch::now_seconds()` must remain the VM's clock and the header timestamp must not be retrofitted into delegation.move's unbonding deadlines without a separate analysis.

7. GENESIS AND LEGACY BLOCKS. `BlockHeader` has `#[serde(default)]` on state_root/receipts_root and `calculate_header_hash` branches on their emptiness (:98). Any node holding blocks written before the fix has headers whose hash was computed under the old rule with an unconstrained timestamp. A header-version field (STEP 0) is mandatory, not cosmetic — without it the STEP 5 replay test cannot distinguish "legacy layout" from "corrupted header", and a chain restart from existing data will fail to reproduce its own history. Decide now whether existing chain data is being kept or the chain is being re-genesised; if kept, v0 verification must be preserved verbatim.

8. TWO BLOCK TYPES, TWO HASH RULES. Fixing `blockchain::Block` while `consensus::Block` (consensus/consensus/src/lib.rs:40-60) still exists with a timestamp-excluding hash and its own `now + 5` proposal check leaves a live second definition of "what a block hash is". Whichever paths still construct it will disagree with the fixed one. Delete or quarantine it in the same change.

GROUND TRUTH OF OUR CODE (mechanism, file:line), with reference-impl contrast where it shapes the fix.

=== BLOCKER-1: atomicity ===
Our mechanism. `AINCOREVM::execute_transaction_actions` (core/vm_move/src/lib.rs:462) opens ONE `session` at :472 and one `AINCOREGasMeter` at :473. The loop at :476 runs each `(action, must_succeed, auth_signer)`. On error, :541-550: if `must_succeed` it `return Err(e)` (session dropped, nothing committed anywhere); otherwise it prints "state reverted", sets `status = ExecutionStatus::aborted(...)` at :547 and falls through. After the loop, :553 `session.finish()` and :554 `changeset_to_kv` return every dirty GlobalValue — including the aborted action's. `changeset_to_kv` (:614-651) maps Op::New|Op::Modify -> `("resource_{addr}_{tag}", Some(hex))` and Op::Delete -> `(key, None)`; it is status-agnostic.
Confirmed against the vendored move-vm at ~/.cargo/git/checkouts/move-5734c3a45f62af74/281f7ec/language/move-vm: `Session` exposes only execute_*/publish_*/finish/finish_with_extensions/load_* (runtime/src/session.rs:72-334) — there is NO checkpoint, snapshot, respawn or rollback API, and `TransactionDataCache::into_effects` (runtime/src/data_cache.rs:75) emits effects for every Dirty GlobalValue. So "revert" is only expressible as "drop the session".
Executor side. `execute_transaction` (core/executor/src/lib.rs:2432) builds `pre_actions` containing exactly one `coin::deduct_gas` action `(action, true, system_address())` at :2693. It then stages the sender/payer AccountData nonce bumps into `updates` directly at :2717-2734 (NOT via the VM). `absorb_vm_result!` (:2739-2757) pushes every `(k,v)` from `vm_changes` into `updates` (:2741-2743), calls `append_supply_tracker_updates` (:2744), and only THEN tests `$status.success` (:2745) to set `tx_status`/`tx_error`. The macro's bool return is used at :2827 and :2928 solely to gate logging and the three post-success mirror helpers (append_validator_set_v1_update :2832, append_validator_removal :2845, refresh_validator_set_v1_stake :2858). The receipt is appended unconditionally at :2959.
Reference contrast. Aptos/Sui both run the prologue (gas/sequence) in a session that is finished and kept, then run the user payload in a SEPARATE session layered on a delta view of the prologue's output; on abort the payload session is dropped and only the prologue changeset plus an epilogue (final gas charge) is committed. Aptos calls this the respawned session / SessionExt with a change-set-backed `Resolver`; Sui's `TemporaryStore` plays the same role. The essential ingredient we lack is the overlay resolver, not a VM feature.

=== BLOCKER-2: conflict tokens ===
`analyze_tx` (core/executor/src/lib.rs:2174) returns `(deps, recognized)`. Always-present tokens: canonical sender (:2188-2191), paymaster (:2203-2208), raw input_objects (:2209-2211). Per-module branches: coin::transfer -> recipient (:2237-2239); staking -> `validator_set_key()` = `resource_0x1_0x1::staking::ValidatorSet` + `sys:validator_set:v1` (:2240-2244); delegation -> ValidatorPool/DelegationRegistry only (:2245-2275); governance -> GovernanceState + VoteEscrow only (:2276-2286); token_factory -> TokenRegistry + TokenWallet only (:2287-2317); dex -> PoolRegistry + pool + LP + sender CoinStores (:2318-2345). Anything else -> `recognized=false` -> `schedule_batches` runs it alone (:2369-2377).
The hole is verified in the Move source: governance.move:52 and token_factory.move:87 both call `staking::burn_ain`, which at staking.move:528-547 does `borrow_global_mut<ValidatorSet>(@0x1)` and `borrow_global_mut<SupplyStats>(@0x1)`. delegation.move:149/228/317/394 call `staking::mint_delegation_reward` (same ValidatorSet) and delegation.move:509 calls burn_ain. None of those three branches declares `validator_set_key()`, and NO branch ever declares `supply_stats_key()` (defined at executor lib.rs:363 but used only by the native mirror).
The collapse happens in `execute_block_parallel`: :1588-1591 runs the batch with `par_iter`, each `execute_transaction` reading only pre-batch RocksDB; :1592 sorts by tx_hash; :1599-1615 folds every tx's updates into one `WriteBatch` with plain `put` — last-write-wins per key; :1620-1631 hashes that merged stream into `sys:state_root`. So the loser's ValidatorSet mutation vanishes while its non-ValidatorSet effects (e.g. withdraw_unbonded's `coin::mint`+`deposit` into `resource_{addr}_CoinStore<AincoreCoin>`, staking.move:331-332) survive. The MAX_SUPPLY tripwire at :995 only warns and only reads the ValidatorSet blob that won.
Reference contrast. Sui derives the conflict set from the transaction's declared object inputs and the runtime aborts on undeclared access; Aptos Block-STM does not declare anything statically — it executes optimistically with a multi-version data structure, records the ACTUAL read/write set per tx, and re-executes any tx whose reads were invalidated. Neither uses a hand-maintained per-module allowlist; the allowlist is only safe if it is a conservative over-approximation of the transitive write set.

=== BLOCKER-3: round fast-forward ===
`current_round` writers: constructor dag.rs:296 (`max(1, max_round+1)`, then `explicit_max_round+1` if `latest_proposed_round` >= that, :277-289), try_create_vertex:562 (+1 after proposing), add_vertex:817 (`= vertex.round + 1` for any remote vertex with `vertex.round > self.current_round`, :816), reload_chain_tip:1865 (`= block.header.round + 1`). `latest_proposed_round` writers: :453, :820, :1868; single reader: :277.
Why +1 is fatal: try_create_vertex:332 takes parents ONLY from `round_index[current_round - 1]`, and :360-379 requires DISTINCT parent authors holding strict >2/3 of stake (`qc::stake_quorum_met`). After a jump to R+2 while the node holds only round-R vertices, round R+1 is empty forever, so `parent_quorum_met` is false forever and the else-branch at :567-612 only re-gossips. The bounds at :637-657 are irrelevant because the harmful jump is +1, far under MAX_ROUND_JUMP=10000.
Reference contrast. Narwhal/Bullshark advance the round only on a locally assembled parent certificate/quorum for round r-1 (`Core::advance_round` fires on a QuorumWaiter result, never on a single peer message); catch-up is done by a certificate-fetch/state-sync loop that back-fills the missing rounds before the round counter moves.

=== BLOCKER-4: commit determinism ===
`try_commit` (ordering.rs:458) sets `anchor_round = current_round - 2` (:479), then loops `attempt in 0..validators.len()` (:504) picking `get_leader_with_fallback(anchor_round, validators, attempt)` (:505, itself deterministic — stake walk over `step1_beacon`, :680-750) and accepts the first leader whose vertex is FOUND IN THE LOCAL `round_index`/`dag` (:508-529). Two nodes with different local availability pick different anchors for the same round, both then satisfy the stake-weighted vote quorum at :556-579 and commit different sequences. The `committed_rounds`/`finalized_round` guard at :487-491 then locks each node into ITS choice permanently.
`find_causal_history` (:752): DFS from the anchor; :763 `if let Some(vertex) = dag.get(&hash)` — a missing parent hash is skipped with no traversal and no deferral; the comparator at :776-793 explicitly handles vertices absent from the dag. So two nodes with different vertex sets produce different `sequence`, hence different `block_txs` (dag.rs:878-886), different tx_hash, different state_root, different `finality_digest` (:623), and different QCs (dag.rs:1010-1030).
Reference contrast. Bullshark/Narwhal commit the anchor for a round only when it is a *certificate* the node has, and the causal-history walk blocks on missing certificates: the ordering layer requests them from the certificate store / peers and defers the commit until the sub-DAG is causally complete. Availability never selects the anchor — the leader schedule plus the certificate is the whole rule.

=== RELATED HIGH A: header hash ===
`Block::new_with_roots` (blockchain/src/lib.rs:46) calls `SystemTime::now()` at :56 and stores it in `header.timestamp` (:69); `calculate_header_hash` (:93) folds `header.timestamp` at :104 (and state_root/receipts_root only when non-empty, :98-101). Sole production call site: dag.rs:911 inside the commit path; `self.latest_block_hash = new_block.header.hash` (:920) then flows into the accumulator (:923), `save_block_json` (:939), and the QC `CommitContext.block_hash` (dag.rs:1013). Recomputation happens in sync `verify_block_hash` (sync/src/lib.rs:81-91, called from validate_block:307) and in the bridge (`depin/bridge-rust/src/aincore_client.rs:50`, where the recomputed hash is bound to the QC at :415-429).
Reference contrast. Aptos/Sui derive block/checkpoint timestamps from consensus metadata (the certified leader/anchor's timestamp, median of validator timestamps), never from local wall clock at block-assembly time.

=== RELATED HIGH B: sync execute-before-verify ===
`process_blocks` (sync/src/lib.rs, loop around 830-1016): validate_block at :965 (structural only — proposer in set, tx_hash, timestamp<now+30, count<=10k, header hash self-consistency); then :974 `executor.execute_block_parallel(...)` which internally takes BLOCK_EXECUTION_LOCK and writes the WriteBatch + `sys:state_root` to RocksDB; only then :976 `verify_execution_roots`, whose failure path just `break`s at :996. `rollback_to_height` (:454-490) deletes `block_{h}` keys and rewinds latest_height/latest_block_hash — it never touches Move resources or `sys:state_root`.

HIDDEN COUPLING / WHY A NAIVE FIX IS DANGEROUS

BLOCKER-1.
- Do NOT "drop the session on abort" wholesale. The single shared session is load-bearing: `coin::deduct_gas` is pushed as `(action, true, system_address())` at executor:2693 and its changeset is the ONLY thing that makes an abort cost money. Drop everything and aborts become free — an unbounded spam vector, and `total_fees` at :1613 (which sums `gas_charged`, not VM state) would then mint proposer fees for gas never actually debited, i.e. you would trade an atomicity bug for a supply bug.
- `bind_signer_args` (vm_move:565) is typed `&Session<'_, '_, AINCOREStorage>`. A second session over an overlay resolver will not typecheck until this signature is generalized. This is the first thing that will break the build.
- The two sessions must NOT double-charge gas: today one `AINCOREGasMeter::new(gas_limit)` (:473) covers all actions. Splitting gives each session its own budget. The executor charges a flat `gas_limit * gas_price` (:2596, :2736) and ignores VM `gas_used`, so this is currently invisible — but any future move to metered gas will silently allow 2x the declared limit.
- Move VM module caching: `MoveVM` (vm_move:147) is created once in `AINCOREVM::new` and its loader caches modules across sessions. An overlay that changes *module* bytes (PublishModule path, executor:2882-2943) will NOT be seen by session B through the loader cache. If you keep publish in the same phase model, verify this explicitly.
- `append_supply_tracker_updates` (executor:975) scans `updates` in reverse for the ValidatorSet key and mirrors `total_supply` into `sys:total_supply` / `total_burned`. If you filter aborted vm_changes out of `updates` you must call it AFTER filtering, or it mirrors a supply value that was never committed.

designs.approach: Adopt Aptos's staged-session pattern in `AINCOREVM::execute_transaction_actions` (/Users/macbookpro/Documents/AINCORE-Blockchain/core/vm_move/src/lib.rs:462-557), replacing the single shared `Session` with PROLOGUE → USER → (reserved) EPILOGUE stages that share ONE `AINCOREGasMeter` and communicate through an owned `BTreeMap<String, Option<String>>` staged write set. Stage 1 runs the leading `must_succeed` pre-actions (today only `coin::deduct_gas`, executor lib.rs:2667-2693) against the raw `AINCOREStorage`, is all-or-nothing (`?` propagates → executor discards the tx, mirroring Aptos's `unwrap_or_discard!` in `execute_user_transaction_impl`), and its ChangeSet is extracted via the existing `changeset_to_kv` into `staged`. Stage 2 runs the user payload in a NEW session created over a new `OverlayStorage` resolver that layers `staged` over the DB — the same ~60-line trick as Aptos's `ExecutorViewWithChangeSet` — so the payload SEES the gas deduction; on the first abort the session is DROPPED and `finish()` is never called, which is the only real rollback the VM has (local `move-vm/runtime/src/session.rs:241` consumes the session in `finish`; `data_cache.rs:75-138` `into_effects` has no provenance and no success flag, and `values_impl.rs:2524-2538` never restores a Dirty GlobalValue to Clean). Because AINCORE's ops are whole-value hex overwrites/deletes over flat string keys, "squash" is plain per-key last-write-wins into the BTreeMap — none of Aptos's aggregator/delayed-field/resource-group complexity applies. Gas on abort is already charged: the executor deducts a flat `gas_limit * gas_price` in stage 1 and sets `actual_gas = gas_cost` ignoring VM `gas_used`, so aborts cost the full declared fee and stage 3 stays an empty, documented slot (to be wired unmetered, Aptos-style `&mut UnmeteredGasMeter`, only if a refund model is ever adopted).
designs.why_this_approach: Filtering the ChangeSet after `finish()` is not merely fragile, it is impossible: `TransactionDataCache::into_effects` emits one Op per (address, StructTag) slot with no record of which action dirtied it, and `deduct_gas` and `coin::transfer` mutate the SAME `CoinStore<AincoreCoin>` GlobalValue — the two writes are literally indistinguishable in the output. Re-running the prologue after a blanket drop is the other tempting fix and is worse: it double-meters, doubles VM work on the abort path (a free DoS amplifier for guaranteed-aborting txs), and Aptos explicitly does not do it — it layers via `ExecutorViewWithChangeSet`. Session splitting is also what makes the wrong thing unrepresentable at the VM boundary instead of relying on every caller to filter, which matters here because three system call sites (`deposit_fee_reward` executor lib.rs:1428-1446, `slash_validator_bps` :2014-2020, `delegation::slash_pool` :2054-2060) currently bind the status to `_` and write the returned changes straight to RocksDB — they have the identical bug and are fixed for free by this change. AINCORE is unusually well-positioned versus Aptos: no self-referential `RespawnedSession`/ouroboros is needed because only the owned write map has to outlive the overlay, so each stage is a plain inline scope.

designs.risks:
"CONSENSUS-BREAKING BY DESIGN: any block containing an aborted tx now produces a different write set, hence a different sys:state_root and receipt hash. Nodes on old and new binaries fork immediately on the first aborted tx. Mitigation is rollout (below), not code.

Compile-time landmines, all verified against the local move-vm at ~/.cargo/git/checkouts/move-5734c3a45f62af74/281f7ec: (1) `bind_signer_args` (lib.rs:566) is hard-typed to `Session<'_,'_,AINCOREStorage>` and MUST become generic over `S: MoveResolver` or stage 2 will not compile; (2) `Session<'r,'l,S>` borrows the resolver, so any attempt to return a session from a helper or store it beside its overlay in a struct is self-referential and will fight the borrow checker — keep each stage inline and let only the owned BTreeMap escape; (3) `MoveResolver` is blanket-impl'd only when ModuleResolver::Error and ResourceResolver::Error are the SAME type, so both OverlayStorage impls must use anyhow::Error.

Loader-cache leakage: the `Loader` lives on `MoveVM`, not on `Session`, so it is the one piece of state that layering does NOT isolate. `flush_loader_cache_if_invalidated()` (move_vm.rs:102) must be called after any stage that published modules, or a published/upgraded module is served stale to the next stage or the next tx in the block.

A metered epilogue would silently reintroduce free aborts: if stage 3 is ever wired onto the shared, near-exhausted meter, an abort that consumed the full gas_limit makes the fee/refund write itself OOG and vanish. It must be unmetered plus asserted (Aptos runs the abort hook with `&mut UnmeteredGasMeter` and then verifies the charge landed). Today stage 3 is empty because gas is a flat up-front burn — do not remove that property without wiring the epilogue first.

Events: `finish()` returns `(ChangeSet, Vec<Event>)` and AINCORE discards events today (`let (changeset, _events)`). When events are wired to the API/indexer they must be captured PER STAGE, so an aborted stage's events die with its writes — an indexer that reports an abort's effects as real is an oracle-poisoning vector (Sui's `drop_writes` explicitly clears events for this reason).

Interaction with BLOCKER-2 (must be fixed with this in hand): stage 1 always writes `resource_{payer}_0x1::coin::CoinStore<0x1::staking::AincoreCoin>`, so EVERY transaction type now provably touches the gas payer's CoinStore. `analyze_tx`'s hand-written per-module dependency sets (executor lib.rs:2174-2330) must include that key for every branch, or the parallel scheduler will batch two txs that both write it. Prefer deriving deps from the actual key set over extending the hand-written lists.

Performance: one extra `new_session` plus BTreeMap inserts per tx. Negligible, and overlay hits are a BTreeMap lookup that short-circuits a RocksDB read.

Residual (out of scope, ticket separately): governance.move:114-118 lets a new vote overwrite `escrow.proposal_id` on a merged escrow from an earlier proposal."
designs.effort: 1.5–2 days. ~0.5 day for overlay.rs + the execute_transaction_actions restructure + generifying bind_signer_args (the borrow-checker scoping is the only fiddly part); ~0.5 day for the 22-site stdlib reorder sweep across 8 .move files plus recompiling the stdlib; ~0.5–1 day for the 9 test groups, the executor tripwire, the three system call sites, and a clean `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`.
designs.rollout: Hard fork of the state-transition function — old and new nodes diverge on the first block containing an aborted transaction. FRESH GENESIS is the clean path and is essentially free here: the audit found that in 349k rounds only 2 blocks carried transactions at all, so there is no meaningful aborted-tx history to preserve, and mainnet has not launched. A coordinated stop → upgrade all 3 machines → restart also works for the same reason; do NOT do a rolling upgrade. Ships INDEPENDENTLY of B2/B3/B4: it touches only core/vm_move (adapter + stdlib) and a narrow slice of core/executor, with no consensus, ordering, or block-header surface. It should ship FIRST — it is the root bug behind the DEX brick, the fund-destruction PoC, and the credit-before-debit mint vectors, and B2's conflict-token fix must be authored with the staged prologue write keys already in place or it will be incomplete on day one. The stdlib reorder sweep can land in the same commit (it is pure defence in depth once the staged sessions exist) or as an immediate follow-up; either way it needs the same genesis/restart event because it changes compiled module bytes.

designs.approach: Two-layer fix, mirroring how Aptos (Block-STM) and Sui (declared object inputs) actually separate "scheduling hint" from "safety". (a) SHIPPABLE NOW — default-deny in `Executor::analyze_tx` (core/executor/src/lib.rs:2174): replace the module-prefix `if/else if` chain (which sets `recognized = true` for ALL of `staking::*`, `governance::*`, `token_factory::*`, `dex::*`) with an explicit per-`(module, function)` allowlist whose token list is derived from the actual Move source, including every 0x1 singleton reachable transitively (`staking::ValidatorSet`, `staking::SupplyStats`, `staking::EmissionPools`, `epoch::Epoch`) plus the two Rust-side derived keys `sys:total_supply` / `total_burned` that `append_supply_tracker_updates` (lib.rs:975) writes whenever `validator_set_key()` appears in the write set. Any 0x1 function not in the table, and every non-0x1 (user-published) module, falls to `modelled=false` and runs alone via the existing singleton-batch path in `schedule_batches` (:2369-2377). (b) DURABLE — capture the REAL footprint at runtime: a `TracingStorage` resolver in core/vm_move/src/lib.rs wrapping `AINCOREStorage` records every `get_module`/`get_resource` key (byte-identical format to `changeset_to_kv` at vm_move/src/lib.rs:623/637), returned alongside the write set; `execute_block_parallel` then validates each batch in BLOCK-INDEX order — a tx whose read∪write footprint intersects a key already committed by an earlier tx in the same batch is deferred and re-executed in a following round. This is Block-STM's validate/re-execute loop minus the MVHashMap, and it demotes `analyze_tx` from a safety boundary to a pure performance hint. Both layers are backed by a commit-time safety net in `execute_block_parallel` (:1599-1615) that detects two distinct tx_hashes staging the same key in one batch and, instead of silently last-write-wins, discards the batch and deterministically re-executes it one tx at a time.
designs.why_this_approach: The current code is unsafe for a structural reason that no amount of adding entries to the table fixes: the write set is hand-written per module while the actual write set is determined by the transitive Move call graph. Verified holes, all reachable today: `governance::create_proposal` (governance.move:52) and `token_factory::create_token` (token_factory.move:87) call `staking::burn_ain`, which `borrow_global_mut<ValidatorSet>` and `SupplyStats` (staking.move:528-546) — neither branch declares them; `delegation::{delegate,undelegate,claim_rewards,distribute_delegation_rewards}` call `staking::mint_delegation_reward`, which `borrow_global_mut<EmissionPools>(@0x1)` (staking.move:495-509) — the delegation branch declares only `ValidatorPool`/`DelegationRegistry`, so two delegation txs to DIFFERENT validators land in one rayon batch, both draw from `delegation_budget`, and last-write-wins restores it: an unbounded mint that is EASIER than the exploit in the audit; `governance::execute_proposal` calls `epoch::update_epoch_duration` (governance.move:185) writing `resource_0x1_0x1::epoch::Epoch`, undeclared; the `staking::*` branch declares `ValidatorSet` + `sys:validator_set:v1` but NOT `SupplyStats`/`EmissionPools`/`sys:total_supply`/`total_burned`, so a staking tx and a burning governance tx collide on the supply mirror. Static `acquires` alone cannot be the durable answer either: `acquires` gives the struct TYPE, not the address (`borrow_global_mut<T>(addr)` takes a runtime value), so a purely static write set would have to lock `CoinStore<AincoreCoin>` type-wide and serialize every transfer — which is why Aptos abandoned static analysis for Block-STM's dynamic read/write sets and Sui requires the tx to DECLARE its objects. Runtime capture is exact, needs no per-module modelling, and cannot drift when a Move module changes. The commit-time detector is the piece that converts a silent consensus fork into a loud, deterministic, self-healing event — the same instinct as Sui re-running `check_conservation_invariants` after `drop_writes` rather than trusting the discard path.

changes.what: (a) `fn schedule_batches(&self, parsed_txs: Vec<(Transaction, String)>) -> Vec<Vec<(Transaction, String)>>` at :2357 — carry the block index and consume TxConflictSet

Body change is mechanical (`let TxConflictSet { tokens, modelled } = self.analyze_tx(&tx);` replacing :2367, `if !modelled` replacing :2369, iterate `tokens` at :2379-2388). The index is what lets the commit loop order by BLOCK POSITION instead of tx_hash — required by (b) and by the fallback in the next item. Caller `execute_block_parallel` :1576 passes `parsed_txs.into_iter().enumerate()`-tagged tuples built at :1561.

changes.what: (a) COMMIT-TIME SAFETY NET: extract the per-batch commit at :1582-1639 into `fn commit_batch(&self, results: Vec<(usize, String, Option<TxExecOutput>)>) -> Result<u128, BatchConflict>` and add cross-tx duplicate-key detection
changes.detail: Inside the new fn, before building the WriteBatch: `let mut writer_of: std::collections::HashMap<&str, usize> = HashMap::new(); let mut conflicts: Vec<(String, usize, usize)> = Vec::new();` then for each (idx, _hash, Some(out)) in block-index order, for each (key, _) in &out.updates: `match writer_of.get(key.as_str()) { Some(&prev) if prev != idx => conflicts.push((key.clone(), prev, idx)), _ => { writer_of.insert(key, idx); } }`. Keying by tx INDEX (not the key alone) is required because one tx legitimately writes the same key twice (e.g. the ValidatorSet mirror then the receipt). If `!conflicts.is_empty()`: write NOTHING, `eprintln!("🚨 [CONSENSUS][B2] batch write-set collision on {} between tx#{} and tx#{} — discarding batch, re-executing serially", ...)` for the first few, and return `Err(BatchConflict { keys, indices })`. In `execute_block_parallel` (:1582 loop), on Err re-execute the batch's txs one at a time, each as its own single-tx `commit_batch` call so tx N+1 reads tx N's committed state. A single-tx batch cannot self-conflict, so recursion depth is 1; if a singleton batch ever returns Err, `panic!` — that is an executor invariant break, not a scheduling miss, and continuing would fork. Determinism argument to put in the comment: every honest node executes the same tx list in the same order, so it derives the same batches, the same conflict set, and the same fallback path; the alarm is deterministic and so is the recovery. Also persist a counter (`sys:sched_conflicts`) inside the same WriteBatch so the event is auditable on-chain rather than only in logs.

changes.what: (a) Replace the tx_hash sort at :1592 with a block-index sort
changes.detail: `results.sort_by(|l, r| l.0.cmp(&r.0))` currently sorts by `tx_hash_hex(raw)` (:1590). That is deterministic across nodes but semantically wrong and grindable: under last-write-wins the tx with the largest SHA256 wins a collision, so an attacker who can pick a nonce/payload byte can decide which of two colliding writes survives. Sort by the block index instead — equally deterministic, and it makes a batch's semantics equal to a sequential run in block order, which is the precondition for the (b) validation loop and for the serial fallback above. designs.risks: "THROUGHPUT: default-deny plus the supply-singleton lock serializes ALL staking, governance, token_factory and burning txs against each other — effectively one such tx per batch. This is correct (they genuinely all RMW `ValidatorSet.total_supply`) and it is what the DEX-era workload needs, but it means those paths no longer parallelize at all. `coin::transfer` and `dex::*` between disjoint accounts/pools keep full parallelism, which is the workload that matters. The (b) validation loop does not recover this either — the contention is real, not modelled. Reducing it needs a Move-level change (per-account burn accumulators settled at epoch boundaries), not a scheduler change. FALSE-NEGATIVE RISK IN (a): the table is still hand-written, so a future Move edit that adds a call to `burn_ain` reopens the hole. That is exactly why the commit-time detector and the acquires-closure CI test are non-optional parts of (a), not follow-ups. DETECTOR FALSE POSITIVES: I checked the shared-key candidates — `tx_receipt:{hash}` and `obj:{addr}` are per-tx/per-sender, `sys:state_root` is written outside the per-tx loop (:1631), `sys:total_supply`/`total_burned` only appear when `validator_set_key()` is in the write set (:975-986) and are then covered by the token. So a cross-tx duplicate key in one batch is always a real modelling bug; no benign case found. If one is later discovered, the fallback degrades throughput but never correctness. LIVENESS: the serial fallback multiplies a conflicting block's execution cost by the batch size. An attacker who finds an unmodelled collision could use it as a mild DoS amplifier (~batch-size work). Bounded by `MAX_OBJECTS_PER_BLOCK`-limited block size and vastly preferable to a fork; mitigate by alarming on `sys:sched_conflicts` so an exploited gap is visible within one block. TRACER OVERHEAD (b): one BTreeSet insert + a String format per resource/module resolution. Meaningful for read-heavy txs; measure with `bench-tps` before/after and consider `HashSet` + a small key cache if it shows up. PANIC PATH: the `panic!` on a singleton-batch conflict halts the node. It is reachable only if a single tx stages the same key under two different tx indices, which is impossible by construction — but it is a halt, so gate it behind an assertion message that names the key and both indices for forensics. INTERACTION WITH B1: B1's staged sessions add gas prologue/epilogue writes. Today those hit the payer's own CoinStore, which is already covered by the always-on payer/sender address token — but if B1's epilogue writes a shared destination (proposer or treasury CoinStore) per tx, that key becomes hot across the entire block and the scheduler will serialize everything. Keep fee accumulation in Rust (`total_fees` at :1613, swept once per block at :1641+) and do NOT move it into per-tx Move state. ADDRESS WIDTH: confirmed `address32` is enabled workspace-wide (core/executor/Cargo.toml:14) so `AccountAddress::LENGTH == 32` and `to_string()` yields the same 64-hex string as `crypto::derive_address` (common/crypto/src/lib.rs:185-193) — the bare-address tokens and the `resource_{addr}_...` keys agree. Any future move to a shorter address must re-verify `sender_token` canonicalization at :2188, or the H2 fix silently regresses."
designs.effort: "(a) minimal safe fix: 1-2 days. ~250 LOC in core/executor/src/lib.rs (key helpers, TxConflictSet, the per-function match, index-tagged schedule_batches, commit_batch extraction + detector + serial fallback) plus ~10 tests. No cross-crate changes, no VM changes, no Move changes. (b) durable fix: 4-6 days on top. ~80 LOC for TracingStorage + VmExecOutput in core/vm_move/src/lib.rs, ~150 LOC plumbing reads through `execute_transaction` and its ~12 test call sites, ~120 LOC for the validation/defer/re-execute loop, ~200 LOC for the acquires-closure CI test. Add 1-2 days if B1 lands first and the tracer has to be threaded through B1's three staged sessions — which it should. Total for both, sequenced after B1: roughly 1.5 weeks including the sequential-equivalence property test that is the real acceptance gate."
designs.rollout: "HARD FORK, both layers. (a) alone changes the state root for any block with more than one tx: the commit order moves from tx_hash to block index (:1592), and the serial-fallback path folds one state root per tx instead of one per batch. (b) changes it again via the defer/re-execute rounds. Neither is backward compatible with a running chain, and there is no migration — the state root is a running fold (:1622-1631), not a recomputable trie root, so nodes cannot re-derive the new root from existing data. FRESH GENESIS IS THE RIGHT CALL, and it is nearly free here: the audit established that in 349k rounds only 2 blocks carried transactions, so there is essentially no history to preserve. Ship (a) and (b) in the same genesis as B1 (atomicity) and B3/B4 (consensus) rather than staging them — every one of these is state-root- or block-hash-affecting, so they collapse into a single restart. INDEPENDENCE: (a) is fully independent of B1/B3/B4 and can be developed and reviewed in parallel; it touches only core/executor/src/lib.rs. (b) is NOT independent of B1 — both restructure the session/resolver boundary in core/vm_move/src/lib.rs, so B1 must land first and the tracer must be built into B1's OverlayStorage rather than bolted on afterwards. Recommended order: B1 → B2(a) → B2(b) → B3/B4 → single fresh genesis. If schedule pressure forces a cut, (a) plus the commit-time detector is the minimum that makes the mint vector unreachable: the detector converts any remaining modelling gap from a silent unbounded mint into a logged, deterministic serial re-execution. Do not ship the DEX before (b) — non-empty payloads are precisely what turns these latent races into live ones. POST-LAUNCH: alarm on `sys:sched_conflicts` != 0; any increment means the hint table has a hole and must be closed the same day even though the detector already contained it."

designs.approach: Make round advance and commit decisions pure functions of the local DAG plus the stake-weighted quorum predicate, exactly as Narwhal (round advance) and Bullshark (anchor commit/skip) specify, and give the node the two mechanisms those rules assume but AINCORE never built: a causal-completeness gate with an orphan buffer, and a vertex-fetch RPC. Four pieces. (1) dag.rs: delete the exogenous fast-forward at :816-821 and derive `current_round` from a new `quorum_round()` — the highest round r whose distinct vertex authors hold >2/3 stake per the existing `crate::qc::stake_quorum_met` — so the node can only ever advance to a round whose predecessor is quorum-complete by construction; the wedge becomes unrepresentable. (2) dag.rs `add_vertex`: enforce the Narwhal parent shape (parents ⊂ round r-1, distinct authors meeting stake quorum, `["genesis"]` at round 1) and buffer — never drop, never insert — any vertex whose parents are unknown above the GC horizon, promoting it when the parents arrive. (3) A new additive `REQUEST_VERTEX:{json}` message whose *response is an ordinary `DAG_VERTEX:` message*, so it reuses `broadcast_vertex`'s exact transport (p2p_tx gossip + `network::send_message` TCP fallback) and needs no new response type or serving path. (4) ordering.rs: replace the round-robin view-change loop at :504-537 with a single deterministic `leader_for_round(r, validators)` that is a pure function of round + validator set (no beacon — the beacon advances per local commit and is itself a fork source), process anchor rounds strictly sequentially via a persisted `next_anchor_round`, decide commit-vs-skip by Bullshark's rule (an undecided anchor is skipped iff it is absent from the causal history of the next committable anchor), and make `find_causal_history` return the missing hashes and DEFER the commit instead of silently skipping them at :755-772. This follows Narwhal/Tusk for round advance and certificate availability, and Bullshark's anchor commit/skip and sub-DAG linearization for ordering; the >2/3 parent quorum AINCORE already has is precisely the quorum-intersection premise the skip rule's safety proof needs.
designs.why_this_approach: The two blockers are one bug with two faces: consensus state is being derived from *local, arrival-order-dependent* observations instead of from the DAG. `current_round` is set from one remote vertex; the anchor is chosen by "whichever leader vertex happens to be here"; the causal walk skips "whatever isn't here". Every alternative fix I considered patches a symptom and leaves the class alive. Raising `MAX_ROUND_JUMP` or clamping the fast-forward still lets a node sit at a round whose predecessor can never fill. Keeping the view-change loop but making it "deterministic" is impossible — its input is local availability. Fixing only the causal walk still lets two nodes pick different anchors. Deriving `current_round` from `quorum_round()` is the same rule Narwhal uses (2f+1 certificates of r before proposing r+1) and it makes the parent-quorum check at dag.rs:360-379 redundant-by-construction rather than a gate that can permanently fail. On leader election specifically: I am removing the VDF beacon from the anchor rule, not weakening it. `update_random_beacon` fires on every local commit, so two honest nodes that have decided a different number of anchors compute different `step1_beacon` and therefore different leaders for the same round — the same class of no-Byzantine-participant fork the code already fixed once at ordering.rs:692-706 by moving election off `last_vdf_output`; the fix stopped one step short. Bullshark ships with round-robin leaders; predictability is a censorship/DoS concern, not a safety one, and the current beacon is already documented as proposer-biasable (audit H-2, deferred). The beacon and the whole QC-fold machinery stay intact for non-consensus randomness. Finally, the orphan buffer plus fetch is not optional polish: the causal-completeness gate turns "silently commit a short sequence" into "stall" unless the node can obtain the missing vertex, and the GC horizon (`finalized_round - 10`, matching the existing prune buffer at dag.rs:1082) is what makes the ancestry recursion terminate.

changes.what: B3 core: replace the remote-vertex fast-forward with quorum-gated round advance
changes.detail: DELETE dag.rs:816-821 (`if vertex.author != self.node_id && vertex.round > self.current_round { self.current_round = vertex.round + 1; put("latest_proposed_round") }`) — this is the wedge and its persistence mechanism. Add `fn quorum_round(&self, round_index:&HashMap<u64,Vec<String>>, dag:&HashMap<String,Vertex>, validators:&[(String,u64)]) -> u64`: highest r in `round_index` whose DISTINCT vertex authors (looked up via `dag.get(h).author`, filtered to the validator set) satisfy `crate::qc::stake_quorum_met(sum_stake, total_stake)`; 0 if none. Add `fn advance_round(&mut self, validators:&[(String,u64)])`: `let target = quorum_round().saturating_add(1); if target > self.current_round { self.current_round = target; }` — monotone, forward-only, never past a non-quorum predecessor. Call it at the end of add_vertex's DAG-insert scope (where the deleted fast-forward was) and at the top of try_create_vertex.

changes.what: B3: separate 'round I signed' from 'round I fast-forwarded to' (anti-double-sign floor)
changes.detail: Add field `last_signed_round: u64` to `DagConsensus`, persisted as new key `consensus:last_signed_round`. Written ONLY in try_create_vertex immediately after `vertex.sign_with_ed25519` succeeds (alongside the existing `latest_proposed_round` write at :450-453, which is KEPT for ops/back-compat but is no longer read as a floor). In try_create_vertex, gate the proposal with `if target <= self.last_signed_round { return; }` where `target = max(self.current_round, quorum_round+1)`. In `DagConsensus::new` (:277-289) replace the `explicit_max_round` floor with: `last_signed = max(storage.get("consensus:last_signed_round"), max round among loaded vertices where vertex.author == node_id)`; `final_start_round = max(1, last_signed + 1)`. Migration is safe because pruning is at `finalized_round - 10` and we sign at `current_round >= finalized_round`, so our own recent signed vertices are always still on disk; log a one-time WARN when legacy `latest_proposed_round` exceeds the derived value and write the new key immediately.

Change the guard at dag.rs:649 from `vertex.round > self.current_round.saturating_add(MAX_ROUND_JUMP)` to `vertex.round > std::cmp::max(self.current_round, self.highest_seen_round).saturating_add(MAX_ROUND_JUMP)`. `ABSOLUTE_ROUND_CEILING` (:631) and `MAX_ROUND_JUMP = 10_000` (:632) are UNCHANGED. changes.what: B3: reload_chain_tip must not push current_round from a synced block
changes.detail: In `reload_chain_tip` (:1858-1870) DELETE the `self.current_round = next_round` / `put("latest_proposed_round")` block. Replace with `self.highest_seen_round = self.highest_seen_round.max(round);`. Height/hash reload at :1837-1843 is unchanged. Rationale: a state-synced node holds blocks but not the DAG vertices for those rounds, so adopting the synced round is exactly the wedge (parents at current_round-1 do not exist locally and never will). The original motivation for that code — the far-future jump guard rejecting live peer vertices — is now served by `highest_seen_round`. Existing test `test_reload_chain_tip_updates_current_round_from_synced_block` (tests.rs:319-350) must be rewritten to assert the new invariant.

changes.what: B3/B4: Narwhal parent-shape validation in add_vertex (permanent reject)
changes.detail: New `fn validate_parent_shape(&self, v:&Vertex, dag:&HashMap<String,Vertex>, validators:&[(String,u64)]) -> ParentCheck` inserted in `add_vertex` after the PWN-001 hash check (:703-711) and the validator-set check (:713-721), BEFORE insertion. Rules: round==1 → parents must be exactly `["genesis"]`; round>1 → parents non-empty, every parent that RESOLVES in `dag` must have `round == v.round - 1` (else permanent reject), and the distinct authors of the resolved parents must satisfy `stake_quorum_met` against the active set (else permanent reject). Returns `ParentCheck::Ok`, `ParentCheck::Reject(reason)`, or `ParentCheck::Missing(Vec<String>)` when parents are merely unknown locally and `v.round - 1 > gc_round`. Honest vertices already comply — try_create_vertex only ever takes parents from `round_index[current_round-1]` (:332-339) — so this is compatible with the running chain going forward and is never applied retroactively (checkpoint/scan replay at :147-260 does not call add_vertex).

changes.what: B3/B4: causal-completeness gate + bounded orphan buffer
changes.detail: New fields: `orphan_buffer: HashMap<String,Vertex>`, `orphans_by_parent: HashMap<String,HashSet<String>>`, consts `MAX_ORPHANS = 4096`, `CAUSAL_GC_DEPTH = 10` (matches the prune buffer at :1082). `fn gc_round(&self) -> u64 { self.ordering_engine.lock().finalized_round.saturating_sub(CAUSAL_GC_DEPTH) }` — a parent whose implied round (`child.round - 1`) is <= gc_round is treated as satisfied even when absent, which terminates the ancestry recursion. On `ParentCheck::Missing(hashes)`: run the existing equivocation check (:747-778) against BOTH `dag` and `orphan_buffer`, then insert into `orphan_buffer` + index under each missing hash, call `request_vertices(&hashes)`, and RETURN WITHOUT inserting into `dag`/`round_index` and WITHOUT persisting. On successful insert of any vertex, drain `orphans_by_parent[new_hash]` into a work queue and re-run `validate_parent_shape` on each, promoting transitively. Eviction: lowest-round-first past MAX_ORPHANS; drop anything with `round <= gc_round`. MOVE the `storage.put("vertex:{hash}")` write (currently at :738-745, before the equivocation check) to AFTER full acceptance, so the DB only ever holds causally-usable vertices and boot replay stays consistent.

changes.what: B3/B4: REQUEST_VERTEX fetch over the existing transport (additive wire message)
changes.detail: Wire: `REQUEST_VERTEX:{"requester":"<node_id>","round":<u64>,"hashes":[..]}`. The RESPONSE is an ordinary `DAG_VERTEX:{json}` — no new response type, so every existing ingest path handles it and un-upgraded nodes ignore the request (main.rs's match falls through to `None`). Requester: `fn request_vertices(&mut self, hashes:&[String])` — dedup via new `pending_fetch: HashMap<String, std::time::Instant>` with `FETCH_COOLDOWN = 2s`, cap `MAX_FETCH_BATCH = 64`, transport copied verbatim from `broadcast_vertex` (:1157-1194): `p2p_tx` gossip via `tokio::spawn` + `network::send_message(addr,&msg)` per peer with `storage.get_peer_ip` resolution. The `round` field keeps the gossip payload unique so gossipsub's sha256 message-id + `duplicate_cache_time = 60s` (p2p.rs) does not swallow retries. changes.detail: Replace `fn get_leader_with_fallback(&self, round, validators, attempt) -> String` (:680-750) with `fn leader_for_round(round: u64, validators: &[(String,u64)]) -> String`: seed = first 8 bytes of `Sha256(b"AINCORE_LEADER_V2" || round.to_le_bytes() || for each (addr,stake) in validators { addr.as_bytes(); stake.to_le_bytes() })`; then the EXISTING cumulative-stake walk over the canonically sorted `validators` (:731-749) unchanged, including the `total_stake == 0` uniform fallback. No `self`, no beacon, no attempt. Rationale is the same class the code already fixed at :692-706 but one step short: `step1_beacon` is refreshed by `update_random_beacon` on every LOCAL commit (:293-305), so two honest nodes that have decided a different number of anchors elect different leaders for the same round. `update_random_beacon`, `fold_qc_for_height`, `mix_qc_into_beacon`, `get_random_beacon` and all their tests are KEPT for non-consensus randomness.

changes.what: B4: sequential anchor decisions with a persisted cursor (kills the arrival-order commit partition)
changes.detail: Add `pub next_anchor_round: u64`, persisted as `consensus:next_anchor_round`, initialised in `new_with_storage` to `finalized_round + 1` (1 at genesis). Rewrite `try_commit` (:458-673): rename the first param to `max_known_round` (arity unchanged); replace the `current_round < 4` guard (:468) and `anchor_round = current_round - 2` (:479) with `let r = self.next_anchor_round; if r + 2 > max_known_round { return None; }`; DELETE the `committed_rounds.contains || anchor_round <= finalized_round` partition guard (:487-491) — it is unreachable once rounds are processed one at a time in order; DELETE the `for attempt in 0..max_attempts` view-change loop (:495-545). Every anchor round is now decided exactly once, in order, on every node, regardless of which vertex arrival triggered the attempt.

changes.what: B4: Bullshark commit-or-skip as a pure DAG function
changes.detail: New body for the decision at round `r`: (1) `leader = leader_for_round(r, validators)`; find its vertex in `round_index[r]`; (2) committable iff present AND the distinct authors of `round_index[r+1]` vertices whose `parents` contain the anchor hash satisfy `stake_quorum_met` — this is the existing vote computation at :551-579, kept verbatim; (3) if not committable, scan forward `r2 in r+1 ..= min(r + MAX_ANCHOR_LOOKAHEAD, max_known_round - 1)` (`MAX_ANCHOR_LOOKAHEAD = 64`) for the first committable anchor; if found, compute its causal history H and SKIP round r iff `anchor_r ∉ H` (authoritative because H is complete down to gc_round — see the completeness gate), incrementing `next_anchor_round` and returning None so the next call decides r+1; if no committable r2 in the window, return None (a pure delay, identical on every node with the same DAG). Safety rests on quorum intersection between the >2/3 anchor support in r+1 and the >2/3 parent quorum every round-r+1 vertex must carry — which the new `validate_parent_shape` rule now enforces at ingest.

changes.what: B4: causal walk must DEFER on a missing parent, never silently skip it

Current defect at :763-771: `if let Some(vertex) = dag.get(&hash)` silently drops unknown hashes and :790-792 even encodes a sort order for them. New rule while descending from a vertex at round `rr`: a parent is satisfied if it is in `dag`, OR in `self.committed_set`, OR `rr - 1 <= gc_round` (implied round below the finality/prune horizon — parents are guaranteed round rr-1 by the new shape rule, so this arithmetic is exact and needs no lookup); anything else is collected into the Err vector. Add `missing_parents: Vec<String>` field + `pub fn take_missing_parents(&mut self) -> Vec<String>` so dag.rs can trigger the fetch. Add `gc_round: u64` as a `try_commit` input derived from `self.finalized_round.saturating_sub(10)`. On Ok, KEEP the existing `(round asc, hash asc)` sort (:776-794) — it is already the correct deterministic linearization once the set is complete — but replace the `(Some,None)/(None,Some)` arms with a defensive `debug_assert!(false)` since missing vertices are now impossible.

designs.risks: "Liveness cost of the single deterministic leader: removing the view-change fallback loop means a round whose leader is down is SKIPPED (correct Bullshark) rather than reassigned, costing ~1 round of latency per down leader, and a >1/3-stake validator going down skips ~1/3 of anchors. This is only acceptable at n>=4; at the current n=3 the >2/3 stake predicate already means f=0 (one node down halts quorum entirely), so n>=4 is a hard prerequisite for this release, not a nice-to-have. Second: the causal-completeness gate converts 'silently commit a truncated sequence' into 'stall' — the chain now depends on REQUEST_VERTEX actually working. If fetch fails (peer_ip unresolved, rate limit too tight, all peers pruned the vertex) commits stall rather than diverge, which is the right failure mode but IS a new liveness surface; mitigations are the 2s retry cooldown, the existing re-gossip fallback at dag.rs:594-611, and the gc_round escape hatch that lets ancestry below finalized-10 be presumed satisfied. Third: the orphan buffer is a new attacker-reachable memory surface — it is bounded at 4096 and, critically, entries are admitted only AFTER signature verification, hash-binding (PWN-001), validator-set membership and the round-jump guard, so filling it requires validator keys. Fourth: dropping legacy latest_proposed_round as the boot floor is the one place where a mistake causes self-equivocation and a 100% slash; the derivation from self-authored on-disk vertices is safe only because pruning is at finalized_round-10 and signing happens at current_round >= finalized_round — if anyone later makes pruning more aggressive this invariant breaks, so it needs an explicit comment and a test. Fifth: enforcing the parent-shape rule at ingest means a mixed-version network partially rejects nothing today (honest vertices already comply) but an un-upgraded validator will still fast-forward ITSELF into the wedge — all validators must upgrade together. Sixth: quorum_round() iterates the round index per call; it is O(rounds retained) and called on every add_vertex, so it must be cached per (round_index generation, validator set) or bounded to a descending scan of the last few rounds, or it becomes a per-vertex CPU cost at 350k rounds."
designs.effort: "5-8 engineering days of implementation plus a mandatory multi-day 4-node soak. Breakdown: dag.rs round advance + last_signed_round + highest_seen_round + reload_chain_tip (~150 lines changed, 1 day); parent-shape validation + orphan buffer + promotion (~200 lines, 1.5 days); REQUEST_VERTEX request/serve + main.rs wiring (~150 lines, 1 day); ordering.rs leader rule + sequential cursor + commit/skip + completeness gate (~350 lines rewritten, 2 days); blockchain.rs + deterministic block timestamp (~40 lines, 0.5 day); tests (~800 lines including the 4-node integration harness, 2 days). The 4-node soak with non-empty payloads is the real long pole and cannot be compressed — it is the only thing that actually exercises B4, since the existing 349k rounds carried payloads in exactly 2 blocks."
designs.rollout: "Hard fork with a FRESH GENESIS — required, and for a reason that is independent of B3/B4: every node's block hashes ALREADY diverge today, because Block::new_with_roots reads SystemTime::now() at consensus/blockchain/src/lib.rs:56 and calculate_header_hash folds header.timestamp at :104, with prev_hash chaining the divergence through the whole history. There is no shared canonical block history to preserve. On top of that, (a) the commit rule changes — single deterministic leader, sequential anchor cursor, causal-completeness gate — produce a different block sequence from the same DAG, so replaying the existing 349k rounds under the new rule yields different blocks, and (b) consensus:next_anchor_round has no valid derivation from the legacy consensus:committed_rounds set. Reset cost is effectively zero: 349k mostly-empty rounds, 2 tx-bearing blocks, no external users, and a locked fair-launch model with no pre-mine to migrate. Independence: B3+B4 share NO files with BLOCKER-1 (core/vm_move, core/executor) or BLOCKER-2 (core/executor::analyze_tx) and can be built on a parallel branch. But they must SHIP together with B1/B2 in one genesis-resetting release — each of the four needs a reset anyway, one reset should cover all of them, and B4's determinism guarantee only becomes observable once payloads are non-empty, which is precisely what B1/B2 unblock. Sequencing within the release: land B1 first (it supplies the staged-change-set mechanism that the sync/src/lib.rs:972-975 commit-before-verify HIGH depends on), then B2, then B3/B4, then cut genesis. Two hard prerequisites for the reset, both already tracked: n>=4 validators (the single-leader skip rule and the >2/3 stake predicate both need f>=1) and systemd auto-start (a reboot froze the current 3-node chain for 10 days)."

designs.approach:
H1 (deterministic header): delete the `SystemTime::now()` in `blockchain::Block::new_with_roots` (consensus/blockchain/src/lib.rs:56) and make `timestamp` a parameter. The value is derived by a new pure `blockchain::bft_block_timestamp(samples, parent_ts)` — a stake-weighted median over the timestamps of the vertices in `commit.sequence` (one sample per author, weight = validator stake), clamped monotonically against the parent block's timestamp. This is Tendermint/CometBFT BFT-Time adapted to our DAG: vertex timestamps are already author-signed (they are inside `Vertex::calculate_hash`, dag.rs:191-203) and already future-bounded on ingest (dag.rs:659-676, MAX_FUTURE_DRIFT_SECS=30), so the median is authenticated input, and a >1/3-honest-stake bound keeps the median inside the honest range. The call site dag.rs:911 collects `(author, stake, timestamp)` in the same DAG-lock loop that already collects payloads (dag.rs:876-887), and `DagConsensus` gains a `latest_block_timestamp` field alongside `latest_block_hash`. `calculate_header_hash`'s preimage layout is unchanged, so every stored block still self-verifies and every existing QC over an existing `block_hash` still verifies — only future block-hash VALUES change, which is a hard fork.
H2 (verify before commit): two layers, mirroring how Aptos separates authentication from execution. (a) Durable fix — never execute an unauthenticated block: `process_blocks` takes the `QuorumCertificate` that already arrives in `SyncResponse.finality` (sync/src/lib.rs:646/676), verifies it with the existing `consensus::qc::verify_qc` against `trusted_validator_set(qc.epoch)` (the identical crypto backstop `apply_finality_artifact` uses at :384-389), and refuses to execute any block with `height > qc.block_height`; at `qc.block_height` the header hash and executed state_root must equal `qc.block_hash`/`qc.state_root`, which retroactively authenticates every prev_hash ancestor below it. (b) Buffered writes — a new `storage::StateView` trait with two impls (`StateDB` = direct, `StagingView` = overlay buffer, same `Some(None) => Ok(None)` staged-delete rule as the BLOCKER-1 overlay resolver). `Executor::new_staged()` returns an executor whose every write lands in the overlay; sync executes, calls `verify_execution_roots`, and only then `staging.commit()` — a single fsync'd batch that also carries the block record. On mismatch it calls `staging.discard()` and literally nothing was written.
designs.why_this_approach: The `session.finish()`-vs-drop lesson from BLOCKER-1 applies one layer up: you cannot filter partial writes out after the fact, you must never put them somewhere they can leak. `execute_block_parallel` commits a fsync'd `WriteBatch` per scheduling batch (core/executor/src/lib.rs:1633) plus ~27 direct `self.db.put/delete` calls in the reward, burn, slash, epoch and governance phases (:1068-2150) — all of which run BEFORE sync's root check at :976. Any fix that leaves the executor writing through to RocksDB is cosmetic. `StagingView` is the same overlay shape BLOCKER-1 needs in vm_move, so the two fixes share one concept instead of inventing two. Making `Executor.db` an `Arc<dyn StateView>` rather than `Arc<StateDB>` makes "write directly to the DB during a staged block" a compile error rather than a review item. On the QC side, all the machinery already exists and is already trusted for finality (`verify_qc` binds chain_id, epoch validator set, set hash, >2/3 stake) — the QC even signs `state_root` and `receipts_root`, so it is a cryptographic terminal check, not a self-consistency check like the current re-execution comparison. The residual noted in the existing comment at sync/src/lib.rs:988-991 ("the complete remediation authenticates blocks BEFORE execution") is exactly this. For H1, BFT-Time over `commit.sequence` is the only timestamp source that is both deterministic (all nodes committing the same sequence see identical vertex hashes, and the timestamp is inside the hash preimage so it cannot be varied per-node) and adversary-bounded (stake-weighted median + the existing 30s future cap), without introducing any new wire field.

changes.what: H1: add the pure BFT-time function and the shared drift constant
changes.detail: New: `pub const MAX_BLOCK_TIME_DRIFT_SECS: u64 = 30;` (shared with dag.rs's MAX_FUTURE_DRIFT_SECS and sync validate_block's hardcoded 30 at sync/src/lib.rs:292) and `pub fn bft_block_timestamp(samples: Vec<(String /*author*/, u64 /*stake*/, u64 /*ts*/)>, parent_timestamp: u64) -> u64`. Algorithm, all deterministic, no clock read: (1) fold samples into one-per-author keeping the max ts for that author (a validator gets exactly one vote even though the committed sequence spans rounds); (2) drop zero-stake authors; (3) sort by (ts, author); (4) weighted median = smallest ts whose cumulative stake satisfies `cum*2 > total`; (5) if no samples, use `parent_timestamp`; (6) return `max(median, parent_timestamp)` — monotonic non-decreasing, NOT strictly increasing (1-second granularity with sub-second rounds makes equal timestamps normal). Deliberately no clamp against local wall clock here: that would reintroduce the non-determinism this change removes. Future drift stays enforced where it belongs — at vertex ingest (dag.rs:670) and at block ingest (sync validate_block:292).

changes.what: H2b (NEW FILE): the StateView trait and the StagingView buffer — the rollback primitive
changes.detail: `pub trait StateView: Send + Sync` with `get(&self,&str)->Result<Option<String>,rocksdb::Error>`, `put`, `delete`, `write_batch_kv(&self, ops: Vec<(String, Option<String>)>) -> Result<(),rocksdb::Error>`, `scan_prefix`, `scan_prefix_limited`, plus default-implemented typed helpers that route through `get` (`get_chain_height`, `get_object`, `get_burn_percentage`, `get_active_validators`, `put_object`, `index_transaction`) so overlay reads see staged values. `write_batch_kv` takes a kv vec rather than `rocksdb::WriteBatch` because a WriteBatch is opaque and cannot be staged; the executor already materialises exactly this vec at core/executor/src/lib.rs:1600-1612 before building the WriteBatch. `impl StateView for StateDB` delegates to the existing fsync'd put/delete/write_batch (common/storage/src/lib.rs:108/135/299) — zero behaviour change on the direct path. `pub struct StagingView { base: Arc<StateDB>, writes: RwLock<BTreeMap<String, Option<String>>> }` with `new`, `discard(&self)` (clear the map — THE rollback), `commit(&self) -> Result<(),rocksdb::Error>` (drain into one `rocksdb::WriteBatch`, one `base.write_batch` = one fsync), `take_writes`. Its `get` is the critical line and the one most likely to be written wrong: `match writes.read().get(key) { Some(Some(v)) => Ok(Some(v.clone())), Some(None) => Ok(None), None => self.base.get(key) }` — a staged DELETE is a HIT, not a fall-through (same trap as pitfall #3 of the BLOCKER-1 overlay: fall-through resurrects deleted resources, e.g. a cleared pending-slash or a removed unbonding entry). `scan_prefix` = base scan merged with overlay entries under the prefix (overlay overrides, `None` removes), re-sorted by key. RwLock not Mutex: the rayon phase does concurrent reads through this view.

changes.what: H2b: VM resolver reads through the same view so staged writes are visible mid-block

designs.risks:
"H1 is consensus-breaking. The header-hash PREIMAGE is unchanged (so stored blocks and existing QCs keep verifying — no data migration, no re-index), but the timestamp VALUE differs, so a node on the new binary and one on the old produce different block hashes from the first new block onward and then fail each other's prev_hash check in validate_block. There is no partial rollout: every validator must cut over at the same height, or with fresh genesis. A gated variant (genesis-pinned `sys:config:bft_block_time_height`) is possible but introduces a dual hashing path forever — not recommended.
H1 BFT-time quality degrades with a tiny validator set. At n=1 the median is that node's own clock (no worse than today). Above ~1/3 malicious stake the median can be skewed, bounded by the existing 30s future cap on vertex ingest and by monotonicity below — i.e. an attacker can pull block time forward at most 30s, never backward. With a validator whose clock is far behind, the monotonic clamp means block time stalls rather than regresses; no liveness impact, but ops should still run NTP.
H2b's refactor surface is 58 executor sites + 3 vm_move sites + ~10 governance sites. The real risk is not the mechanical edits, it is MISSING a component that still holds a raw `Arc<StateDB>` and writes through it during a staged block (governance was one; a future one is likely). Mitigated structurally by typing `Executor.db` as `Arc<dyn StateView>` (direct writes become compile errors) and behaviourally by the key-set-snapshot escape test.
StagingView adds an RwLock read on the VM's hot resource-read path. The direct path (`StateDB`) is unaffected, but measure the staged path with `cargo run -p bench-tps` before enabling staging on the consensus commit path.
StagingView buffers a whole block in memory; bounded by MAX_OBJECTS_PER_BLOCK=10_000 and the 10k tx cap in validate_block:300, so worst case is tens of MB. Acceptable, but do not reuse it for multi-block batching.
H2a changes sync liveness semantics: a node whose peers serve no verifiable QC stops advancing once `require_qc_sync` is on. That is the correct trade (better stuck than corrupted), but it makes QC production a hard mainnet dependency — the qc_producer path must actually be producing complete QCs with n>=4 validators before the flag is flipped, otherwise the network cannot sync at all.
The reorg path (sync/src/lib.rs:881-928) still cannot undo executor state — `rollback_to_height` only deletes block records, as its own comment at :882-890 admits. H2b does not fix that (it buffers one block, not a range). The QC anchor rule makes the case unreachable in practice (you never execute past certified finality), but a full per-height state-undo log remains open work.
Staging must never be applied to the peer/vertex/checkpoint keys other node components write concurrently. It isn't, because a StagingView is scoped to one Executor instance — but anyone tempted to add a global 'staging mode' flag on StateDB would roll back unrelated concurrent writes. Call it out in the module doc."
designs.effort: "~4-5 engineer-days total. H1: ~0.5 day (the constructor + BFT-time fn + dag.rs call site are small; most of the time is updating ~20 `Block::new` call sites in sync/src/tests.rs and consensus/consensus/src/tests.rs and writing the determinism tests). H2a (QC-before-execute): ~1 day — all crypto already exists, it is wiring `authenticated_anchor` + three refusal rules + the config knob + 4 tests. H2b (StateView/StagingView refactor): ~2-3 days — new storage module ~150 lines, then mechanical edits across executor (58 sites), vm_move (3 sites), governance (~10 sites), plus the differential and escape-hatch tests. Sequencing note: H2b's overlay is conceptually the same object as BLOCKER-1's `OverlayStorage`; doing BLOCKER-1 first and reusing the type saves roughly half a day and avoids two divergent overlay implementations."
designs.rollout:
"H1 is a HARD FORK. No block-format field is added and no stored artifact is invalidated (preimage unchanged ⇒ old blocks and old QCs still verify), but block hashes diverge from the activation point, so it requires a coordinated cutover. Recommendation: ship it at the fresh-genesis mainnet cutover — the same cutover that flips the already-provisioned `sys:config:require_exec_roots` (sync/src/lib.rs:58-65). No migration, no dual code path, no activation-height logic. If the existing 349k-round testnet must survive, the alternative is a genesis-pinned activation height with a legacy branch, which I would not carry into mainnet.
H2b (staged writes) is NOT consensus-breaking and NOT a wire-format change: identical state_root, identical receipts_root, identical block bytes — the only difference is WHEN the same bytes hit disk. It can land on the running testnet immediately and independently of H1, and it is the piece that stops the bleeding.
H2a (QC-before-execute) is also wire-compatible (`SyncResponse.finality.qc` already exists and is already served, sync/src/lib.rs:352-357), but its enforcement flag `sys:config:require_qc_sync` must stay OFF until QC production is live with n>=4 validators — otherwise sync halts network-wide. Ship the code now with the flag off; flip it at the fresh-genesis cutover alongside `require_exec_roots` and `tip_agreement_n`.
Suggested order: BLOCKER-1 overlay → H2b (shares the type, ships to testnet at once) → H2a (ships dark, flag off) → H1 (fresh genesis only). H1 and H2 are independent; neither blocks the other."

plan.executive_summary:
Verified against source: all four blockers are real as described. `execute_transaction_actions` (core/vm_move/src/lib.rs:462-556) unconditionally calls `session.finish()` after an abort and returns the partial changeset; `absorb_vm_result` (core/executor/src/lib.rs:2739-2757) pushes those writes into `updates` before reading `status.success`, and the batch commit loop (:1595-1633) writes them into a RocksDB WriteBatch and folds them into `sys:state_root`. `analyze_tx` (:2174+) hand-writes per-module dep sets while `schedule_batches` (:2357-2394) batches on those sets and the commit loop is last-write-wins per key (:1599-1612). `dag.rs:816-820` sets `current_round = vertex.round + 1` from one remote vertex while `try_create_vertex` (:331-379) takes parents only from `current_round - 1` behind a stake-weighted quorum gate. `ordering.rs:493-510` picks the anchor by round-robin over whichever leader vertex happens to be local, and `find_causal_history` (:752-770) silently skips parents missing from the local DAG. Confirmed extras: `blockchain/src/lib.rs:56` bakes `SystemTime::now()` into the header hash at the sole call site `dag.rs:911`, and `sync/src/lib.rs:974` calls `execute_block_parallel`, which commits to RocksDB internally (:1633), BEFORE `verify_execution_roots` at :976.

The plan is 12 steps in dependency order. Atomicity ships first because it is the root of the DEX brick, the fund-destruction PoC and the credit-before-debit mints, and because the staged prologue adds write keys (the gas payer's CoinStore) that the B2 conflict-token fix must already know about. Header determinism ships before the consensus work because you cannot verify B3/B4 fixes — or fix the sync verify-before-commit hole — while every node derives a different block hash for identical content. B3 (liveness) before B4 (safety) because a wedged chain cannot produce the payload-carrying blocks that B4's determinism gate needs to be tested against.

One fresh genesis is required, once, immediately before burn-in (Step 11). It is essentially free: the audit found only 2 of 349k rounds carried transactions, and mainnet has not launched. A second genesis is only needed if a state-transition change lands after burn-in begins.

The single largest risk is not any individual blocker: it is that the payload execution path has effectively never run. `bench-tps/src/main.rs:62` still emits the legacy string payload `"transfer:{to}:1:{nonce}"`, which the BCS-only mempool rejects — so there is currently no tool on this machine capable of putting real load on the code these fixes touch. Building that tool is Step 2 and it gates every "done when" that follows.

sequenced_plan.title: B1 — staged sessions + overlay resolver (transaction atomicity)
sequenced_plan.why_this_order: Root cause of the proven fund-destruction PoC, the permanent DEX pool brick, and the credit-before-debit mint class. It also changes the write-key footprint of EVERY transaction (stage 1 always writes the gas payer's CoinStore), so B2's conflict tokens must be authored with it already in place or they ship incomplete on day one. It touches only vm_move + a narrow executor slice — no consensus surface — so it can land and be verified independently. Grounded in the local move-vm source: Session owns its TransactionDataCache and finish(self) consumes it (runtime/src/session.rs:241); into_effects (runtime/src/data_cache.rs:75-138) emits one Op per slot with no provenance and no success flag; GlobalValueImpl::into_effect (types/src/values/values_impl.rs:2524-2538) never restores a Dirty value to Clean and mark_dirty fires at the mutating instruction. Therefore drop-without-finish is the ONLY rollback the VM has, and filtering the returned ChangeSet is structurally impossible — deduct_gas and coin::transfer mutate the same CoinStore GlobalValue and are indistinguishable in the output. Aptos solves the identical must-survive/may-abort split with PrologueSession -> UserSession -> EpilogueSession layered over ExecutorViewWithChangeSet (aptos_vm.rs ~2138, failed_transaction_cleanup :620-887); AINCORE needs no ouroboros RespawnedSession because only the owned write map must outlive the overlay.

Plus: the executor tripwire (`!status.success && pre_actions.is_empty() && !vm_changes.is_empty()` -> refuse the tx) is wired at both user call sites, and the three system call sites that bind status to `_` (deposit_fee_reward :1428-1446, slash_validator_bps :2002-2020, delegation::slash_pool :2039-2060) now log a loud SYSTEM_TX_ABORT instead of silently no-opping. cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings clean.

Doing them after Step 1 (not before) means each fix can be tested with the atomicity guarantee actually in place. sequenced_plan.title: B2a — default-deny conflict tokens in analyze_tx (ship-now layer)
sequenced_plan.why_this_order: Depends on Step 1: the staged prologue means every tx provably writes resource_{payer}_CoinStore<AincoreCoin>, which must be a declared token on every branch. The current structure sets recognized=true for whole module prefixes (staking::*, governance::*, token_factory::*, dex::*) while declaring only that module's own resources — but the governance and token_factory branches both reach staking::burn_ain, which borrow_global_mut's ValidatorSet and SupplyStats. Two such txs land in one rayon batch (:2384-2391), each reads pre-batch DB state, and the commit loop's per-key last-write-wins (:1601-1612) lets one ValidatorSet blob erase the other — the unbounded-mint exploit. Replace the prefix chain with an explicit per-(module, function) allowlist whose tokens include every transitively reachable 0x1 singleton (staking::ValidatorSet, staking::SupplyStats, staking::EmissionPools, epoch::Epoch) plus the Rust-derived sys:total_supply / total_burned keys that append_supply_tracker_updates writes. Anything not in the table — including all user-published modules — falls to recognized=false and runs alone via the existing singleton path (:2371-2377). This is Sui's model: the read/write set is declared up front and anything undeclared is serialized, never optimistically parallelized.
sequenced_plan.done_when: (a) A differential test executes a fixed 500-tx block twice — once through schedule_batches, once forced fully serial — and asserts byte-identical sys:state_root and receipts_root; run over 100 randomized mixes including the exploit pairing (staking::withdraw_unbonded + a hash-ground token_factory tx). (b) test_b2_withdraw_unbonded_cannot_be_replayed: the specific exploit is executed 100 times in a row and total AIN supply is unchanged apart from the emission schedule; the unbonding entry does NOT reappear. (c) A guard test asserts every allowlist entry includes the gas-payer CoinStore token, so a future branch cannot forget it. (d) Under Step 2's load generator at 50 TPS for 30 minutes, zero batch-conflict tripwire hits.

sequenced_plan.title: B2b — runtime read/write footprint tracing + batch validation & re-execution (durable layer)
sequenced_plan.why_this_order: Step 4 is correct only as long as the hand-written table stays in sync with the Move source; the next stdlib change silently invalidates it. This step demotes analyze_tx from a safety boundary to a pure performance hint, which is what Block-STM does (Gelashvili et al., 'Block-STM: Scaling Blockchain Execution by Turning Ordering Curse to a Performance Blessing'): execute optimistically, VALIDATE against what earlier transactions actually wrote, re-execute on conflict. Ship it after Step 4 rather than instead of it, so the chain is never blocked on the harder change. A TracingStorage resolver wrapping AINCOREStorage records every get_module/get_resource key (byte-identical to the keys changeset_to_kv already emits at vm_move/src/lib.rs:623/637) and returns the read set alongside the write set; execute_block_parallel then validates each batch in BLOCK-INDEX order and defers-and-re-executes any tx whose read∪write footprint intersects a key already committed by an earlier tx in the same batch.
